PostgreSQL, plain SQL, safe to run any number of times:

```sql
-- migrate_users_split_name.sql
BEGIN;

ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS first_name text;
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_name  text;

-- Backfill only rows not yet migrated, so re-runs are no-ops.
-- First whitespace-delimited token -> first_name, remainder -> last_name.
-- ponytail: naive split ("Mary Ann Smith" -> "Mary" / "Ann Smith"); names aren't
-- reliably splittable, so let users correct their own afterwards.
-- ponytail: single UPDATE locks every touched row; batch by id range if the table is large.
UPDATE users
SET first_name = substring(btrim(full_name) FROM '^\S+'),
    last_name  = coalesce(substring(btrim(full_name) FROM '^\S+\s+(.*)$'), '')
WHERE first_name IS NULL
  AND full_name IS NOT NULL
  AND btrim(full_name) <> '';

COMMIT;
```

Check it on a scratch table before pointing it at real data:

```sql
CREATE TEMP TABLE users (id int, full_name text);
INSERT INTO users VALUES (1,'Ada Lovelace'),(2,'  Cher '),(3,'Mary  Ann Smith'),(4,NULL),(5,'');
\i migrate_users_split_name.sql
\i migrate_users_split_name.sql   -- second run must change nothing
SELECT id, first_name, last_name FROM users ORDER BY id;
-- expect: (Ada,Lovelace) (Cher,'') (Mary,Ann Smith) (NULL,NULL) (NULL,NULL)
```

Skipped: dropping `full_name`. Run `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS full_name;` as a separate migration once the app reads and writes the new columns, because it's irreversible. Also skipped: `NOT NULL` constraints, which you can add after rows with NULL or empty names are handled. Using MySQL or SQLite instead? Tell me and I'll swap the regex calls.
